g-apg-glossary.title: Agile Practice Guide glossary: agile terms and definitions
g-apg-glossary.notes: Acronyms: ATDD, BDD, BRD, DA, DoD, DoR, DSDM, Evo, LeSS, LSD, PDCA, PMO, ROI, RUP, SAFe, SBE, XP. Key definitions for lessons and items: A3 (problem-solving on a single A3 sheet); ATDD (collaboratively creating acceptance criteria and tests before delivery); agile (a mindset of values and principles per the Manifesto); agile coach; agile life cycle (both iterative and incremental); agile mindset (four values and twelve principles); anti-pattern (known flawed pattern of work); backlog refinement (progressive elaboration of requirements, collaboratively reviewing, updating and writing them); BDD (test-first design and validation using English-like scripts); blended agile (two or more frameworks or practices together, e.g., Scrum with XP and Kanban); I-shaped (single deep specialism), T-shaped (one deep specialism plus broad ability), broken comb or paint drip (various depths in multiple skills); burndown (work remaining vs time left in a timebox) and burnup (work completed toward a release); cadence (rhythm of execution); collective code ownership; continuous delivery and continuous integration; cross-functional team; daily scrum/standup; definition of done (criteria for a deliverable to be ready for customer use) vs definition of ready (information needed to begin work on a requirement); DevOps (collaboration of development and operations for smooth flow); double loop learning (challenges underlying values and assumptions to find root causes) vs single loop learning (applies predefined methods without challenging them); Evo (credited as the first agile method, focused on multiple measurable value requirements); fit for purpose vs fit for use; flow master (Kanban coach, equivalent to scrum master) and service request manager (orders requests to maximise value, equivalent to product owner); Hoshin Kanri (strategy/policy deployment); hybrid approach (glossary wording: combination of agile and non-agile elements 'having a non-agile end result' - unusual wording, lessons describe hybrid as a combination of approaches without that clause); IDEAL improvement model (initiating, diagnosing, establishing, acting, learning); impact mapping; impediment/blocker; increment (functional, tested, accepted deliverable that is a subset of the outcome); incremental life cycle (finished deliverables usable immediately) vs iterative life cycle (feedback on unfinished work to improve it); information radiator; iteration (timeboxed cycle doing all work needed to deliver value); kaizen events; kanban board; mobbing (many members on one work item) vs swarming (many members resolving one impediment) vs pair work; organisational bias (exploration vs execution, speed vs stability, quantity vs quality, flexibility vs predictability); organisational change management; personas; pivot (planned course correction testing a new hypothesis); PDCA; predictive approach and predictive life cycle (bulk of planning up front, single pass); product backlog (ordered list of user-centric requirements); product owner (maximises product value, accountable for the end product); refactoring (improve design without altering behaviour); retrospective; rolling wave planning; scrum board; scrum master (coach and process owner, removes obstacles, facilitates events, shields the team); Scrum of Scrums; Scrum team (glossary says development team, scrum master and 'process owner' - conflicts with Annex A3.2, which names the product owner; lessons follow A3.2); self-organising team (people fluidly assume leadership); servant leadership; siloed organisation vs value stream; smoke testing; specification by example; spike (short fixed-length research or prototyping interval to prove viability); sprint, sprint backlog, sprint planning; story point (unit-less relative estimate); technical debt (deferred cost of work not done earlier); test-driven development; timebox (fixed period, e.g., 1 week to 1 month); user story (brief description of value for a specific user - a promise for a conversation); user story mapping; UX design; value stream mapping.
